items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Our first night in the Apple, we had dinner with a Swiss friend, named Peter Wydler and his wife Othella. I was their best man when they married in Paris, France in 1949.

ctx.x: served was never very well seasoned and was not the same as that which was served in the main dining room. The Indian employees ate in the same dining room as we did but they had special food cooked in curry.

The head waiter was named Peter and like most of the waiters he was from Goa which was a part of India governed by Portugal. We told Peter that we liked curried food better than what we were getting and when they had some left over, Peter looked out for us and curried food was never wasted.

One thing I had a hard time to get used to was Lizards. They were everywhere and in the best hotels and houses. In our place they were almost as thick as flies, our beds had screens to protect us from mosquitos, but there was no protection to keep lizards out of the house. They were about two-and-a-half inches long with tails almost twice as long as the body and are known as wall lizards.
